why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository. Everything they name exists at this commit: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, the test files, the README, package-lock.json (needed for `npm ci`) and the root and package `npm test` scripts. The setup's printf strings have no % signs, so the fixtures are written as intended and later commands only use files it creates. The checks use only standard shell: `; echo "exit=$?"`, `2>/tmp/jv104/err.txt`, pipes and `cd packages/jsonl-lint && node --test 2>&1 | tail -40`. The gh calls use real flags and JSON fields (number, headRefOid, files, body, url) and a valid search. The trailing `--` in `gh pr diff <number> ... --` is harmless, and `<number>` is plainly a placeholder. On the JavaScript side, `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')`, `process.argv.slice(2)` and spawnSync's `input` option are all valid Node. Every command would run as written.
